slides.title: emails that make new clients feel **looked after**
slides.sub: A welcome sequence you write once and reuse, with the 3 prompts.

steps.d: Day 0. Thanks, what happens next, how to reach you.
Day 2. A short checklist, one deadline.
Day 7. Progress, how you'll work, one question.

cards.title: Welcome
cards.text: Write a welcome email for a new client of my [BUSINESS]. Include: a thank you, the next 3 steps with dates: [STEPS + DATES], and how to reach me: [CONTACT + HOURS]. Warm, under 120 words.

slides.note: Example business, invented: a one-person bookkeeping service.

messages.text:
Subject: Welcome! Here's what happens next

Hi Maria,

Thanks for choosing me to look after your books. Here's what happens next:
1. By Friday: I'll send a short list of what I need.
2. By the 31st: your accounts are set up.
3. On the 1st: your first monthly summary.

Questions? Email me any time. I reply within one working day, Mon–Fri.

Ben

cards.title: What I need
cards.text: Write a short email asking my new client for: [LIST]. Use a checklist, with a few words on why I need each. One clear deadline: [DATE].

cards.title: Week-one check-in
cards.text: Write a check-in email for a client one week in. Say what's done: [PROGRESS]. How we'll work from now on: [ROUTINE]. End with one question: is there anything you'd like done differently? Under 80 words.

messages.text:
Subject: 4 things I need to get started

Hi Maria, to set up your books I need:
• Bank statements, last 3 months (to match payments)
• Sales invoices since January (to record income)
• Receipts for business costs (to record expenses)
• Read-only access to your invoicing app (to keep it in sync)

Could you send these **by Friday the 23rd**? Thanks!
Ben

slides.kicker: Email 3 · the one most people skip

after.label: WEEK ONE, WITH THE TEMPLATE
after.text: Hi Maria, one week in! Your accounts are set up and September is fully matched. From now on, you'll get a summary on the 1st of each month. Is there anything you'd like me to do differently?

slides.note: One question at the end. Small problems come up early, while they're easy to fix.

caption:
Client onboarding email templates: a 3-email welcome sequence (with AI prompts)

Three short emails make them feel looked after:

1) Day 0, Welcome:
"Write a welcome email for a new client of my [BUSINESS]. Include: a thank you, the next 3 steps with dates: [STEPS + DATES], and how to reach me: [CONTACT + HOURS]. Warm, under 120 words."

2) Day 2, What I need:
"Write a short email asking my new client for: [LIST]. Use a checklist, with a few words on why I need each. One clear deadline: [DATE]."

3) Day 7, Check-in:
"Write a check-in email for a client one week in. Say what's done: [PROGRESS]. How we'll work from now on: [ROUTINE]. End with one question: is there anything you'd like done differently? Under 80 words."

Save them as templates and swap names and dates. Keep client details out of the chat and add them after.
